candidate.name: Clarum
candidate.description: AI agents for private market diligence, monitoring, and reporting
candidate.long_description:
Clarum automates diligence, monitoring, and reporting for private market investors. Our AI agents learn how each firm works and automate their process end to end. Everything is individualized (checklists, templates, scoring models) and adapts as your process changes.

Clarum also acts as a self-updating knowledge base across every document your firm has ever seen, connecting dots no analyst could.

score.thesis: AI-native autonomous agents owning high-value business workflows

analysis.team: Two-person team led by founder/CEO Anton Otaner (YC profile lists team size 2, though only one founder is named) [YC profile; Founder bio: Anton Otaner]. Otaner's prior experience is technically adjacent: blockchain infrastructure at Mint and augmented reality product development at EPHAS, an Ericsson One startup [Founder bio: Anton Otaner]. His bio references co-founders but the second founder is not named or profiled in the sources. No explicit background in private markets, finance, or diligence is described, which is notable given the domain.
analysis.product: Clarum builds AI agents that automate diligence, monitoring, and reporting for private market investors [YC one-liner; YC long description]. The agents learn how each firm operates and automate the process end to end, with individualized checklists, templates, and scoring models that adapt as a firm's process changes [YC long description]. It also functions as a self-updating knowledge base across every document a firm has seen, surfacing connections across them [YC long description].
analysis.market: Target market is private market investors, positioned within B2B, Fintech, and Finance/Accounting SaaS [YC tags]. The sources give no market size, no named customers, no pricing, and no competitor information, so market size and competitive landscape are unknown. A why-now is implied only by the AI-agent framing (agents that 'connect dots no analyst could') but the sources provide no traction or timing evidence [YC long description].
risks: Autonomy is asserted but unproven: the product is described as automating 'end to end,' yet the sources contain no evidence of how autonomous the agents actually are in practice [YC long description; score breakdown notes no explicit autonomy language].

Small, thinly-documented team — team size 2 with only one founder named and no stated finance/private-markets domain expertise, a demanding sector for diligence tooling [YC profile; Founder bio: Anton Otaner].
No momentum or traction signals in the sources: no customers, revenue, hiring, or usage data available [score breakdown; sources contain none].
Launched 2024-03-11, over a year ago, with no visible progress signals since — raises questions about growth pace [Signal: Launched 2024-03-11].
what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence of paying private-market firms using Clarum end-to-end, with retention or workflow-ownership metrics.
Clear demonstration of genuine agent autonomy (agents completing diligence tasks with minimal human intervention) rather than assisted automation.
A named, credible second founder or team members with private-markets/finance domain depth.
analysis.recommendation_rationale: Clarum fits the thesis on AI centrality and workflow ownership — AI agents owning diligence, monitoring, and reporting for private market investors [YC long description] — but the sources lack proof of autonomy, traction, and momentum, and the team is small with no stated finance-domain expertise [score breakdown; Founder bio: Anton Otaner]. The 52/100 score reflects a strong-on-paper thesis fit undercut by missing autonomy and momentum evidence. Warrants a Watch: track for traction and autonomy proof points before leaning in.
